description: How scripts/cmux-next/oracle/gen_tla.py turns TLC simulate traces of these specs into tests/oracle/corpus/tla/ cases (p15-oracle-100). Each action is one disjunct of the spec's Next with its bound variables; gen_tla.py writes a trace module that EXTENDS the spec, keeps Next as the step relation and labels every step with the action that took it (a step no action here explains is a generator error, so this map covers Next exactly). An action maps to `owner` (the spec's owner op, which gen_tla.py turns into resource-operations-v2 calls by its op kind under `ops`), `restart` (the daemon restarts on the same state root), `internal` with the reason it has no product step (client mirror, view or channel state), or `unmapped` with the reason no product op exists. An op kind marked `unmapped` has no product op: a trace that applies it is dropped and counted in coverage.json. A config's `constants` replace the .cfg's values for the simulation. A spec with `excluded` makes no cases: its configs only check that the map labels every Next step, and coverage.json lists it as excluded with that reason. `view` names client view state no product checks yet (`viewExcluded` says which follow-up does); the daemon facet has none. `restartRace` is a daemon defect after an owner restart: gen_tla.py keeps `keep` cases per spec with one racing call, each under a `[ Pass Failure ]` line it writes to tests/oracle/Expectations.d/tla.txt, and drops and counts the other racing cases.

restartRace.why: after a daemon restart the terminals adopt on their own threads; a tab.move on a tab still adopting fails nondeterministically with operation.failed layout-conservation-violation (the layout reducer disagrees with the live move), and no event or read tells a client the adoption ended

actions.label: Issue
actions.why: the client builds an op from its own mirror; the product call is the owner's Process of it

actions.label: Sync
actions.why: the client adopts the owner's state and repairs its focus and top rows (client view state)

actions.label: Focus
actions.why: the client moves its own focus (client view state; the owner never reads it)

actions.label: Replay
actions.why: a used key arrives again; the product call is the owner's Process of it, sent with the same idempotency key

split.why: split inside the row: pane.split right on the anchor

newcol.why: new column after the anchor's column: pane.split right with viewport_width; only a full-height row (h = MaxH) is a daemon column

move.why: append to the destination pane (the own pane's end when it is the source)

dock.why: dock a live column of a screen in columns mode; its column_id comes from a screen.get just before

newrow.unmapped: rows-v1 New Row has no resource-operations-v2 op (only cmux-tui's legacy new-row command, server.rs NewRow)

torow.unmapped: rows-v1 move tab to a new row has no resource-operations-v2 op

pinrow.unmapped: edge docks of layout-model.md (FRAME = TRUE) have no resource-operations-v2 op

orient.unmapped: the frame orientation of layout-model.md (FRAME = TRUE) has no resource-operations-v2 op

actions.label: StartDrag
actions.why: a drag gesture hides the tab in the client's strip (DP1 drag presentation)

actions.label: CloseTab
actions.why: the client logs a close intent and sends it; the product call is the owner's apply of it

actions.label: CancelDrag
actions.why: a cancelled gesture sends nothing

actions.label: DropSplit
actions.why: the client logs a split intent; the product call is the owner's apply of it

actions.label: DropMove
actions.why: the client logs a move intent (or releases an own-place drop); the product call is the owner's apply of it

actions.label: DropTearOff
actions.why: the client logs a tear-off intent; the product call is the owner's apply of it
actions.excluded: a trace whose tear-off reaches the owner is dropped (op tearoff has no product op), and in 1,000 simulated traces of TabLayout_fixed.cfg none lost its tear-off before the owner applied it

actions.label: Receive
actions.why: the client applies (or drops) an owner batch into its mirror

actions.label: ReceiveSettled
actions.why: the client ends an intent on request-settled

actions.label: Reconnect
actions.why: the client takes a snapshot and resends its pending intents; a resend reaches the owner as a keyed replay

actions.label: Disconnect
actions.why: a client connection drops; the owner's state is unchanged

actions.label: DuplicateBatch
actions.why: the event channel delivers a batch twice to one client
actions.excluded: client channel only (the owner and so the daemon facet never see it), and TLC's random simulation took it in none of 1,000 traces of TabLayout_fixed.cfg: the one fault of MaxFaults = 1 goes to Disconnect, OwnerRestart or ReplayRequest first

actions.label: ReplayRequest
actions.why: a request is sent again with its key; the product call is the owner's apply of it

move.why: MoveTab, including the own pane and the own index

split.unmapped: SplitWithTab has no resource-operations-v2 op: pane.split always starts a new terminal in the new pane

tearoff.unmapped: MoveToNewWorkspace (tear-off) has no resource-operations-v2 op: workspace.create starts its own terminal or none

actions.label: Close
actions.why: anyone closes pane p: pane.close

actions.label: Focus
actions.why: the person focuses pane p: pane.focus

actions.label: Create
actions.why: a new focused column right after the focused one: pane.split right with viewport_width and focus

actions.label: Animate
actions.why: the presented scroll offset steps toward its target (client view state)

actions.label: Resync
actions.why: the client settles unchanged geometry again (client view state)

closefocus.view: focus: the window's focused pane after FocusAfterClose.pane (close-focus.md). The daemon's active pane is not the window's focus, so a daemon run checks the columns only; the app's layout facet (the active screen's focusedPane) could check it, but driver_app.py runs no resource.call step. The scroll target and offset are not in any facet.
closefocus.viewExcluded: #26009: no product checks the focus after a close yet; the app variant of these cases (action.run steps on named panes, checked against focusedPane) is the follow-up

actions.label: IssueAny
actions.why: the client logs an intent and sends it; the product call is the owner's Commit of it

actions.label: Retry
actions.why: a timeout resends a pending intent with its key; the product call is the owner's answer to it

actions.label: Disconnect
actions.why: a client connection drops with its in-flight messages

actions.label: Reconnect
actions.why: the client resends every pending intent with its key and asks for a snapshot

actions.label: OwnerSnap
actions.why: the owner answers a snapshot request (a read)

actions.label: SettleHeld
actions.why: the client settles a held reply once its mirror covers it

actions.label: ReceiveSnap
actions.why: the client adopts a snapshot

actions.label: ReceiveDelta
actions.why: the client applies a delta (keep: the channel duplicates it)

actions.label: ReceiveSettled
actions.why: the client receives request-settled (keep: the channel duplicates it)

actions.label: OwnerReceive
actions.why: a decided key is a keyed replay of its first call; an undecided one is only staged until Commit

actions.label: Commit
actions.why: the owner commits the staged op: its product call

actions.label: OwnerRestart
actions.why: the store is durable; the staged op and every connection are lost

move.why: move to the end of a pane that holds tabs; the model keeps empty panes, the daemon removes them

move-to-empty-pane.unmapped: the model keeps an emptied pane and moves a tab into it; the daemon has no empty pane to name (an emptied pane is removed in the same commit), and moving a tab into a new pane has no resource-operations-v2 op

write.unmapped: a client-owned record write needs the writer's connection identity; the case driver has one connection (a second identified connection is p15-oracle-237's user connection)

FeedHandoff.excluded: the handoff is between the daemon's local feed server and FeedDO (cloud-api), and the oracle's daemon runs offline with no FeedDO; the local feed verbs are daemon commands, not resource-operations-v2 ops

actions.label: LocalAnswer
actions.why: the user answers the item at the local feed server (a daemon feed command, not a resource-operations-v2 op)

actions.label: StartHandoff
actions.why: the local server freezes the item and sends feed.adopt to FeedDO, which the offline oracle has none of

actions.label: Resend
actions.why: the local server resends feed.adopt with key adopt:<id> to FeedDO

actions.label: LocalMoved
actions.why: the local server records moved after FeedDO's result

actions.label: TimeoutUnfreeze
actions.why: the Unfreeze mutant only (Unfreeze = FALSE in every config here)

actions.label: CloudAnswer
actions.why: the user answers at FeedDO (cloud-api)

actions.label: CloudAdopt
actions.why: FeedDO commits the adopt or replays it from its ledger (cloud-api)

actions.label: Lose
actions.why: the network loses a message (channel state)

actions.label: WaiterLocal
actions.why: an agent's cmux feed watch reads the local owner and follows owner.moved (a daemon feed command)

actions.label: WaiterCloud
actions.why: the watch reads the answer at FeedDO (cloud-api)

hovercard.excluded: HoverCardMachine.swift is app view state driven by the pointer, the timer and scroll or drag suppression; no resource-operations-v2 op, daemon state or app facet carries it, and driver_app.py has no pointer step

actions.label: Hit
actions.why: a hit test under the pointer (moved or not): pointer input, no product op

actions.label: Deadline
actions.why: the card timer fires or a stale token arrives (the machine's own timer)

actions.label: Dismiss
actions.why: Escape or a click dismisses the card: pointer and key input on the card, no product op

actions.label: Suppress
actions.why: a drag or scroll starts (pointer input)

actions.label: Unsuppress
actions.why: a drag or scroll ends (pointer input)

actions.label: Removed
actions.why: the target under the card leaves the view (a geometry change the machine observes)

actions.label: Pin
actions.why: a click pins the card for t (pointer input)
